## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why

`muse_spark_rmsnorm` is one `local_compile` boundary shared by every residual-stream norm, with `recompile_limit=16` sized for pretraining's 12 graphs. An RL trainer runs the model in more ways: a `no_grad` log-prob pass and a training pass, over micro-batches of varying token counts. On Muse Spark with the `dapo_math` recipe's LoRA setup the first training step dies with `FailOnRecompileLimitHit` in that boundary (fullgraph=True makes the 17th graph a hard failure).

Measured on an 8xH200 box with `TORCH_LOGS=recompiles` over two rollouts (Muse Spark 4-layer slice, TP2/EP2, rank-32 attention LoRA, log-prob and training passes), graphs per boundary:

| boundary | graphs | limit |
|---|---|---|
| `muse_spark_rmsnorm` | 22 | 16 -> 32 |
| `muse_spark_attention_qk` | 8 | 16, unchanged |

The rmsnorm graphs split on: weight present or not, weight width 8192 or 4096 (expert space), FSDP-wrapped or plain module type, input token count, and `requires_grad` of the input (log-prob vs training pass).

## What changed

One line plus its comment: `muse_spark_rmsnorm` compiles with `recompile_limit=32`, following the per-boundary convention (`models/common/rope.py` does the same for DeepSeek-V4 with 32). This replaces the earlier `LocalCompileConfig.recompile_limit` knob from this PR's first revision, which no recipe set.

## Numerics / performance

No numerics change: the same graphs compile, the limit only stops the 17th from raising. With the raised limit the RL run completes two rollouts and two training steps with the regions on.

## Testing

- The measurement run above completes end to end with the limit raised; on the pinned v0.4.0 it fails at the first training step.
- No new test: the failure is a hard error at the first step of any RL run on this model, which cannot come back silently.

**Verdict: Request changes** -- the problem is real, but the fix adds a global knob that no recipe sets, so the in-repo Muse Spark RL recipe still fails. The codebase's convention is to give each boundary a limit that covers RL (see `rope.py`).

**What this PR does.** It adds `LocalCompileConfig.recompile_limit`, a floor applied to every `local_compile` boundary and to every always-compiled helper. A boundary that declares a higher limit keeps it. `_compile` becomes an instance method so it can read the floor, and out-of-tree overrides now have to call `self._compile_kwargs(...)` to pick it up.

**Example.**
```
# Muse Spark RL (dapo_math recipe): a no_grad log-prob pass plus a training pass
# over varying token counts
muse_spark_rmsnorm: 12 graphs (grad) + 12 (no_grad) + dynamic-size recompiles > 16
  main:     FailOnRecompileLimitHit (fullgraph=True)
  this PR:  still fails unless the recipe sets
            config.model.local_compile.recompile_limit = 32, and no recipe does
  proposed: @local_compile("muse_spark_rmsnorm", ..., recompile_limit=32)
            with the graph count in the comment; works for every trainer, no knob
```

1. `torchtitan/distributed/local_compile.py:27-30` -- the new field has no consumer, and per-boundary limits are the existing convention. Raise the limit on the boundary that fails instead (see inline).
2. `torchtitan/distributed/local_compile.py:41` -- if the field stays, apply the floor in the bind callbacks so `_compile` overrides can't drop it without anyone noticing (see inline).

### Should consider
- `torchtitan/distributed/local_compile.py:46-48` -- reads the private `torch._dynamo.config.recompile_limit` without a TODO.
- `torchtitan/distributed/local_compile.py:17` -- removes a blank line, which is unrelated to this change.
- `tests/unit_tests/cpu/config/test_compile_config.py:206` -- the new test only checks a `max()`. If the boundary-level fix replaces the field, delete the test and revert the change to the example subclass.

### Questions
- Was `muse_spark_attention_qk` seen failing too, or only `muse_spark_rmsnorm`? Raise only the boundaries that are measured to fail, and write the graph count in each comment.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- The RL recipe for Muse Spark (`torchtitan_recipes/rl/dapo_math.py:236`) builds the model with the default `local_compile.regions` (`torchtitan/models/muse_spark/model.py:440-453`), which include `muse_spark_rmsnorm`. So the failure described in the PR can happen in-repo, and this PR doesn't change that recipe.
- `models/common/rope.py:192-200` is the precedent: its comment counts the call sites, the doubling from no_grad, the recompiles from a second token count, and the other code paths, then sets 32. Raising each failing boundary the same way keeps the reasoning next to the code. A global floor raises every boundary, including ones that don't need it, so an unexpected recompile storm somewhere else gets hidden.
- Size of the smaller alternative: about 2 decorator edits plus their comments, with net LoC close to 0, compared with +62/-5 here.

</details>

Not verified: the exact number of graphs `muse_spark_rmsnorm` compiles in the RL run (this needs a GPU run). A maintainer still needs to review.

This knob has no in-repo consumer. No recipe sets it, so `muse_spark_816b_a42b_dapo_math_gb300_config` (`torchtitan_recipes/rl/dapo_math.py:236`) uses the default regions, including `muse_spark_rmsnorm`, and still hits `FailOnRecompileLimitHit` after this PR.

It also goes against the per-boundary convention in `models/common/rope.py:192-200`. That comment counts the graphs a boundary needs, including the doubling from no_grad calls and the extra graphs a second token count adds, and sets the limit to cover all of them (32). How would a user pick a value for a single global floor across boundaries with very different graph counts?

Smaller fix that needs no knob: raise `muse_spark_rmsnorm` (and `muse_spark_attention_qk` if it also fails) to 32, and say in the comment why: 12 graphs, times 2 grad modes, plus the dynamic-size recompiles. That's about 2 lines of code plus the comments, and it deletes this field, `_compile_kwargs`, and the test.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the item below before merging** -- the global knob is gone. The fix is now the per-boundary limit raise that the last review asked for, and the comment records the measured graph count.

**What this PR does.** It raises `muse_spark_rmsnorm`'s `recompile_limit` from 16 to 32. The new comment explains the count: 12 graphs for pretraining, and 22 measured for an RL trainer, which also runs a `no_grad` log-prob pass and micro-batches with varying token counts.

**Example.**
```
# Muse Spark RL, dapo_math LoRA setup: log-prob (no_grad) pass + training pass
muse_spark_rmsnorm graphs: 22
  main:    limit 16 -> FailOnRecompileLimitHit at the first training step (fullgraph=True)
  this PR: limit 32 -> run completes; same graphs, no numerics change
muse_spark_attention_qk graphs: 8, limit 16 unchanged
```

### Earlier review: status
- Global `LocalCompileConfig.recompile_limit` knob with no consumer -- resolved (removed; the boundary's own limit is raised instead, following `models/common/rope.py:192-200`).
- Floor applied inside the overridable `_compile` hook -- resolved (removed along with the knob).
- Private `torch._dynamo.config.recompile_limit` read, unrelated blank-line removal, and the `max()`-only test -- resolved (all removed).
- Whether `muse_spark_attention_qk` also fails -- answered: it compiles 8 graphs, so it keeps 16.

### Must fix
1. PR description -- the "Summary (human-written)" section is empty. The author has to write it (CONTRIBUTING.md, "AI-assisted contributions").

### Questions
- The 22 count comes from a 4-layer slice with TP2/EP2. The in-repo recipe `muse_spark_816b_a42b_dapo_math_gb300_config` (`torchtitan_recipes/rl/dapo_math.py:260-266`) runs FSDP 8 / TP 4 / EP 16. Can that layout add graph variants, e.g. FSDP-wrapped vs. plain module type on more norms? If so, would it push `muse_spark_rmsnorm` past 32? The same question applies to the regions still at the default limit of 8 (`muse_spark_input_scaled_rmsnorm`, `muse_spark_attention_output`, `muse_spark_residual`, `muse_spark_logit_postprocess`). The measurement run shows they fit in the slice; it doesn't show they fit under the recipe's layout.

Not verified: graph counts under the gb300 recipe's parallelism (needs a GPU run). A maintainer still needs to review.

**Example.**
```
# Muse Spark RL (dapo_math recipe): a no_grad log-prob pass plus a training pass

muse_spark_rmsnorm: 12 graphs (grad) + 12 (no_grad) + dynamic-size recompiles > 16

  proposed: @local_compile("muse_spark_rmsnorm", ..., recompile_limit=32)
            with the graph count in the comment; works for every trainer, no knob
```
